newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Regrade narrows further.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Regrade narrows further.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade narrowed further late afternoon on Tuesday as physical jet fuel was weighed down by fears of a prompt overhang, traders said.
"The regrade came off further this afternoon. I think people are worried over a physical overhang." one trader said.
The August regrade was last quoted at 35/50 cents per barrel, down from 40/60 cents on late Monday prices and down sharply from Friday's $0.85/$1.00, brokers said.
The September regrade also lost ground and was last quoted at 85/95 cents against Monday's $0.85/$1.00, they said.
Late Monday, outright August jet fuel swaps traded at $23.10 when August gas oil traded at $22.70, giving a regrade value of 40 cents, brokers said.
Traders said the fall in the regrade value was triggered by the absence of a Singapore trader from the local spot physical market late last week.
The local trader has over the past two weeks bought several jet fuel cargoes--giving the market a much needed boost at a time when regional demand was at a low.
Lower prices were also down to an increase in stocks after refiners maximised jet production earlier in the month in response to the much wider regrade then.
Jet fuel traded on Tuesday at $23.40 per barrel but offers at $23.00 on Monday failed to draw out any buying interest.

Gas oil swaps edged down slightly late afternoon in quiet trading after picking up slightly earlier in the afternoon on news that Shell Singapore was extending its more than 15 percent crude run cut into August.
Shell said it was maintaining the almost 17-percent cut in refinery output effective since June 27 until market conditions improved.
August gas oil swaps were last quoted down 10 cents from Monday at $22.55/$22.65. August traded earlier in the day at $22.75 before edging down, brokers said.
Fuel oil was also quoted steady with August seen at $99.00/$99.75 per tonne.
